title.en: Channel capacity and multiplexing: how fast one line can go, and how many people share it
title.zh: 信道容量与多路复用：一条线最多传多快，很多人怎么分

description.en: Work out what sets the speed limit of a channel (Nyquist and Shannon), do calculations that involve decibels, and see how time-division and frequency-division let many people share one line.
description.zh: 弄清一条信道的速度上限由什么决定 (奈奎斯特与香农)，会做带分贝的计算题，并懂得时分、频分两种方式怎样让很多人共用一条线。

name.en: Maximum data rate of a noiseless channel: Nyquist's theorem
name.zh: 无噪声信道的最大数据速率：奈奎斯特定理 (Nyquist's theorem, noiseless channel)

name.en: Maximum data rate of a noisy channel: Shannon's theorem and signal-to-noise ratio
name.zh: 有噪声信道的最大数据速率：香农定理与信噪比 (Shannon's theorem, signal-to-noise ratio)

name.en: Using both formulas: take the smaller of the two limits
name.zh: 用两个公式做题：取两个上限里较小的那个 (applying Nyquist and Shannon)

name.en: Three link directions: full-duplex, half-duplex, simplex
name.zh: 链路的三种方向：全双工、半双工、单工 (full-duplex, half-duplex, simplex)
多路复用：时分与频分 (multiplexing: TDM and FDM)
奈奎斯特与香农其人 (Nyquist and Shannon: background)

name.en: Maximum channel data rate and message latency
name.zh: 信道最大数据率与消息延迟 (Nyquist, Shannon, latency)

description.en: Treating the bandwidth B (in Hz) as a data rate (bits/sec), forgetting that the formula itself is what turns Hz into bits/sec.
description.zh: 把带宽 B (单位 Hz) 当成数据速率 (bits/sec)，代公式时忘了公式本身就把 Hz 变成了 bits/sec。

description.en: Plugging 20 dB straight into Shannon's formula as S/N = 20, without first converting it to 100.
description.zh: 把 20 dB 直接当成 S/N = 20 代入香农公式，没有先换算成 100。

description.en: Thinking the rate can grow without limit just by adding more signal levels V.
description.zh: 以为只要不断增加电平数 V，速率就能无限提高。

description.en: Using only one formula on a combined problem; in reality both Nyquist and Shannon must hold, so you take the smaller.
description.zh: 做综合题时只用一个公式；实际上要同时满足奈奎斯特和香农，取较小的那个。

description.en: Confusing capacity (how many bits per second) with latency (how long until it arrives), and thinking a higher rate shortens propagation time.
description.zh: 把容量 (一秒送多少比特) 和延迟 (多久到) 混为一谈，以为提高速率就能缩短传播时间。

description.en: Equating 'can go both ways' with 'can go at the same time', and treating half-duplex (taking turns) as full-duplex.
description.zh: 把「能双向」等同于「能同时」，把半双工 (轮流) 当成全双工。

description.en: Thinking that in time-division multiplexing a user with no data automatically hands the slot to others; under a fixed schedule an empty slot just stays empty.
description.zh: 以为时分复用里没数据的用户，时隙会自动让给别人；固定时间表下空槽就是空着。

title.en: How fast can one phone line go
title.zh: 一条电话线最多能传多快

prompt.en: An old telephone line passes a band about 3 kHz wide. The line uses only two levels, high and low, for 1 and 0, and there is no noise at all. How many bits per second do you guess it can carry at most?
prompt.zh: 老式电话线能通过的频带大约 3 kHz 宽。线上只用高、低两个电平表示 1 和 0，而且完全没有噪声。你猜每秒最多能送多少个比特？

label.zh: 3000 个，一个 Hz 送一个比特

feedback.en: Close, but half too few. The fastest change on the line is alternating high and low, and one cycle holds two symbols.
feedback.zh: 接近了，但少了一半。线上最快的变化是一高一低交替，一个周期里装得下两个码元。

label.en: 3000000, since kHz means a thousand times more

feedback.en: kHz is a unit of frequency, not a factor of a thousand on the bit count. The bit rate depends on how many symbols per second the receiver can tell apart.
feedback.zh: kHz 是频率的单位，不是在给比特数乘一千。比特速率由每秒能分辨多少个码元决定。

label.en: No limit; with clever enough coding it can go as fast as you like
label.zh: 没有上限，编码聪明一点想多快都行

feedback.en: With only two levels each symbol carries 1 bit, and how many times per second the symbol can change is capped by the bandwidth. Coding cannot change that.
feedback.zh: 只用两个电平时，每个码元只有 1 个比特；而码元每秒能换多少次，被带宽封住了。编码改变不了这一点。

explain.en: The answer is 6000. Next we see why it is twice the bandwidth, and then how to go faster when there is no noise.
explain.zh: 答案是 6000。接下来先看为什么是带宽的两倍，再看没有噪声时怎样继续提速。

title.en: Two people, one question

text.en: Every bit your laptop sends ends up as some change on a wire, in light, or in the air. The faster the changes, the harder it is for the other end to make them out. Does a channel have a speed limit? What decides it?
text.zh: 你笔记本发出的每个比特，最后都变成线上、光里或空气里的某种变化。变得越快，对面越来不及看清。一条信道有没有速度上限？由什么决定？

text.en: Two engineers answered it, one after the other. **Nyquist** (Harry Nyquist, 1889-1976, physicist and electrical engineer) studied the basic limits on the bandwidth that communication needs: with no noise, how fast can a channel of bandwidth B carry data? **Shannon** (Claude Shannon, 1916-2001, known as the father of information theory) asked the next question: in the real world there is noise, so how much of that limit is left?
text.zh: 两位工程师先后回答了它。**奈奎斯特** (Harry Nyquist, 1889-1976，物理学家、电子工程师) 研究通信所需带宽的基本极限：没有噪声时，带宽 B 的信道最多送多快。**香农** (Claude Shannon, 1916-2001，被称为信息论之父) 追问下一步：现实里有噪声，上限还剩多少？

title.en: The thread of this lesson

body.en: First use Nyquist to find the speed with no noise, then use Shannon to see how much noise pushes it down. Finally, see how that speed is divided when many people share one line.
body.zh: 先用奈奎斯特算出没有噪声时的速度，再用香农看噪声把它压低多少。最后看很多人共用一条线时，这个速度怎么分。

title.en: Why 2B: the fastest change is two symbols per cycle
title.zh: 为什么是 2B：最快的变化一周期两个码元

text.en: A channel of bandwidth B (in Hz) can pass changes of at most B cycles per second. The fastest a digital signal can change is an alternating 1010... pattern: one high, one low, which is exactly one cycle.
text.zh: 带宽 B (单位 Hz) 的信道，能通过的最快变化是每秒 B 个周期。数字信号变得最快的样子是 1010... 交替，高一下、低一下，正好是一个周期。

svg.en: <svg viewBox='0 0 640 230' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif'><rect width='640' height='230' fill='#fbfbf8'/><path d='M50,70 H140 V140 H230 V70 H320 V140 H410 V70 H500 V140 H590' fill='none' stroke='#222' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M50,48 V40 H230 V48' fill='none' stroke='#b4402a' stroke-width='2'/><text x='140' y='30' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle' fill='#b4402a'>One cycle = 2 symbols</text><g font-size='16' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'><text x='95' y='172'>1</text><text x='185' y='172'>0</text><text x='275' y='172'>1</text><text x='365' y='172'>0</text><text x='455' y='172'>1</text><text x='545' y='172'>0</text></g><text x='320' y='210' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'>At most B cycles per second, so at most 2B symbols per second</text></svg>
svg.zh: <svg viewBox='0 0 640 230' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif'><rect width='640' height='230' fill='#fbfbf8'/><path d='M50,70 H140 V140 H230 V70 H320 V140 H410 V70 H500 V140 H590' fill='none' stroke='#222' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M50,48 V40 H230 V48' fill='none' stroke='#b4402a' stroke-width='2'/><text x='140' y='30' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle' fill='#b4402a'>一个周期 = 2 个码元</text><g font-size='16' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'><text x='95' y='172'>1</text><text x='185' y='172'>0</text><text x='275' y='172'>1</text><text x='365' y='172'>0</text><text x='455' y='172'>1</text><text x='545' y='172'>0</text></g><text x='320' y='210' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'>每秒最多 B 个周期，所以每秒最多 2B 个码元</text></svg>

alt.en: An alternating high-low square wave, with two symbols in each cycle, one high and one low
alt.zh: 交替的高低方波，每个周期里有两个码元，一高一低

caption.en: Symbols cannot change faster than the highest frequency the channel can pass.
caption.zh: 码元换得再快，也快不过信道能通过的最高频率。

text.en: This is the same idea as the sampling theorem in the **Physical layer** lesson. To recover a wave with highest frequency $f_H$, you must sample at least $f_s \ge 2 f_H$ times per second. Turned around: a channel of bandwidth $B$ can tell apart at most $2B$ independent values per second.
text.zh: 这和 **物理层** 一课的采样定理是同一个道理。要还原最高频率 $f_H$ 的波，每秒至少采样 $f_s \ge 2 f_H$ 次。反过来：带宽 $B$ 的信道，每秒最多分辨 $2B$ 个独立的值。

title.en: Two meanings of 'bandwidth'

body.en: Here B is the frequency width of the channel, in Hz. In the Physical layer lesson, 'bandwidth' meant a data rate, in bits/sec. The formula's job is exactly to turn Hz into bits/sec.
body.zh: 这里的 B 是信道的频率宽度，单位 Hz。物理层一课里说的 bandwidth 是数据速率，单位 bits/sec。公式的作用，正是把 Hz 变成 bits/sec。

title.en: Nyquist's theorem: the noiseless channel
title.zh: 奈奎斯特定理：无噪声信道

intro.en: Bits per second = symbols per second x bits carried by each symbol. Work out the two factors separately.
intro.zh: 每秒能送的比特数 = 每秒的码元数 × 每个码元装的比特数。两项分别算。

why.en: From the previous page: each cycle can be split into only two symbols.
why.zh: 上一页：每个周期只能分出两个码元。

why.en: If the signal has V levels, there are V possible states. With V = 2 a symbol is 1 bit, with V = 4 it is 2 bits, with V = 8 it is 3 bits.
why.zh: 信号有 V 个电平，就有 V 种状态。V = 2 时一个码元 1 比特，V = 4 时 2 比特，V = 8 时 3 比特。

why.en: Multiply the two factors; this is Nyquist's theorem.
why.zh: 两项相乘，这就是奈奎斯特定理。

why.en: A 3 kHz binary signal (V = 2): first convert kHz to Hz, and you get 6 kbps, matching the prediction at the start.
why.zh: 3 kHz 的二进制信号 (V = 2)：先把 kHz 换成 Hz，得 6 kbps，与开头的预测一致。

outro.en: There are only two ways to go faster: widen B, or add more levels V. Doubling the bandwidth doubles the rate; doubling the number of levels adds just 1 bit per symbol.
outro.zh: 要更快只有两条路：加宽 B，或增加电平数 V。带宽加倍，速率就加倍；电平数加倍，每个码元只多装 1 个比特。

title.en: Compute a noiseless line

prompt.en: A noiseless channel has a bandwidth of 4 kHz and the signal has 8 levels. What is the maximum data rate in bits/sec?
prompt.zh: 一条没有噪声的信道，带宽 4 kHz，信号有 8 个电平。最大数据速率是多少 bits/sec？

hints.en: First find how many bits each symbol carries: $\log_2 8$.
hints.zh: 先算每个码元装几个比特：$\log_2 8$。

hints.en: Then multiply by the number of symbols per second, $2B$, with B in Hz.
hints.zh: 再乘每秒的码元数 $2B$，B 要用 Hz。

explain.en: Each symbol carries $\log_2 8 = 3$ bits, and at most $2\times 4000 = 8000$ symbols fit per second, so $8000\times 3 = 24000$ bits/sec.
explain.zh: 每个码元 $\log_2 8 = 3$ 个比特，每秒最多 $2\times 4000 = 8000$ 个码元，共 $8000\times 3 = 24000$ bits/sec。

title.en: Can we keep adding levels

prompt.en: Each symbol carries $\log_2 V$ bits. So if we raise the number of levels V to 256, 1024 ......, can't the rate be as fast as we like? What do you think stops it in practice?
prompt.zh: 每个码元能装 $\log_2 V$ 个比特。那把电平数 V 加到 256、1024 ......，速率岂不是想多快有多快？你觉得现实里什么会挡住它？

label.en: Nothing stops it, as long as the equipment can be built
label.zh: 什么也挡不住，只要设备造得出来

feedback.en: That holds only on an ideal channel with no noise. A real line always has noise.
feedback.zh: 那只在没有噪声的理想信道里成立。真实的线上总有噪声。

label.en: Noise: the levels get so close that a small jitter makes it impossible to tell which level it was
label.zh: 噪声：电平挤得太近，噪声一抖就分不清是哪一级

label.en: The wire overheats and burns out

feedback.en: Heat is an engineering problem, not the root of the limit. The real wall is that the receiver cannot read the signal clearly.
feedback.zh: 发热是工程问题，不是上限的根源。真正的墙是接收方读不清。

label.en: The bandwidth B shrinks as V grows
label.zh: 带宽 B 会随着 V 变小

feedback.en: B is a property of the channel itself and has nothing to do with how many levels you pick.
feedback.zh: B 是信道本身的性质，和你选几个电平无关。

explain.en: Right, it is noise. The next page uses a picture to show how it muddles the levels.
explain.zh: 对，是噪声。下一页用一张图看它怎样把电平搅混。

title.en: Noise: more levels are harder to tell apart

text.en: The receiver reads the signal in a simple way: it checks which level the received voltage is closest to. Noise adds onto the signal and makes the voltage wobble.
text.zh: 接收方读信号的办法很朴素：看收到的电压离哪一级最近。噪声会叠在信号上，让电压晃来晃去。

alt.en: On the left, two levels whose noise bands are far apart; on the right, four levels whose neighbouring noise bands overlap
alt.zh: 左边两个电平，各自的噪声带分得很开；右边四个电平，相邻噪声带互相重叠

caption.en: The blue bands are the range the voltage may wobble over because of noise. With the total swing fixed, more levels mean smaller gaps.
caption.zh: 蓝色带是噪声让电压可能晃到的范围。总摆幅不变，电平越多，间距越小。

text.en: The total swing is set by the signal power and is limited. The more levels there are, the smaller the gap between neighbouring ones. Once the noise wobble exceeds half a gap, the receiver reads wrongly.
text.zh: 总摆幅由信号功率决定，是有限的。电平越多，相邻两级间距越小。噪声晃动一旦超过半个间距，接收方就读错。

text.en: Another figure in the slides shows the same thing: take the same 0/1 waveform. With weak noise (large SNR), you can still tell high from low after the noise is added; when the noise is as strong as the signal (small SNR), the combined waveform is a mess and even 0 and 1 are hard to tell apart.
text.zh: 课件里的另一张图是同一件事：同样的 0、1 波形，噪声弱时 (大信噪比，large SNR)，叠加后仍看得出高低；噪声和信号一样大时 (小信噪比，small SNR)，叠加后的波形一团乱，连 0 和 1 都难分。

title.en: So V cannot grow forever
title.zh: 所以 V 不能无限加

body.en: Noise puts a ceiling on how many levels can be told apart. Shannon gave an exact answer for how high that ceiling is.
body.zh: 噪声给「能分辨多少级」划了顶。这个顶有多高，香农给了精确答案。

title.en: Shannon's theorem: the limit that noise pushes down
title.zh: 香农定理：噪声压低的上限

text.en: Each term handles one thing:
text.zh: 两项各管一件事：

items.en: **B**: how fast the signal can change (Hz). The wider the channel, the faster it changes.
items.zh: **B**：信号能变多快 (Hz)。信道越宽，变得越快。

items.en: **$\log_2(1+S/N)$**: how many levels can be told apart at each instant, expressed in bits. The larger S/N, the more levels can be seen clearly.
items.zh: **$\log_2(1+S/N)$**：每个时刻能分辨多少级，用比特数表示。S/N 越大，能看清的级越多。

items.en: **S/N**: the ratio of signal power to noise power, an ordinary number with no unit.
items.zh: **S/N**：信号功率与噪声功率之比，是一个没有单位的普通比值。

text.en: Take the worst case: signal and noise equally strong, $S/N = 1$, $\log_2 2 = 1$. Then each Hz carries only 1 bit per second.
text.zh: 举个最差的情形：信号和噪声一样强，$S/N = 1$，$\log_2 2 = 1$。这时每个 Hz 每秒只能送 1 个比特。

text.en: Note that the formula has **no number of levels V**. V is the coding you choose; Shannon gives a wall that no coding can get past. So adding more levels does not help.
text.zh: 注意公式里 **没有电平数 V**。V 是你选的编码方式；香农给的是不管怎么编码都越不过的墙。所以电平再多也没用。

title.en: Beyond the slides: where the wall is and whether you can reach it
title.zh: 超出课件：墙在哪、够不够得着

body.en: Set $2B\log_2 V = B\log_2(1+S/N)$ and you get $V=\sqrt{1+S/N}$. With a signal-to-noise ratio of 100, $\sqrt{101}\approx 10$, so you hit the wall at around 10 levels. Also, Shannon's figure is a theoretical limit that only ideal coding can approach; real systems fall short of it.
body.zh: 令 $2B\log_2 V = B\log_2(1+S/N)$，得 $V=\sqrt{1+S/N}$。信噪比为 100 时，$\sqrt{101}\approx 10$，电平加到 10 个左右就碰到墙了。另外，香农给的是理论上限，要靠理想的编码才能逼近，实际系统达不到。

title.en: Decibels: another way to write the signal-to-noise ratio
title.zh: 分贝：信噪比的另一种写法

text.en: The signal-to-noise ratio spans a huge range (from 1 to several million), so engineers often write it in decibels (dB). Problems usually give dB, but the formula wants the plain ratio.
text.zh: 信噪比的数值跨度太大 (从 1 到几百万)，工程上常用分贝 (decibel, dB) 来写。题目给的往往是 dB，公式要的却是普通比值。

text.en: The rule is easy to remember: every 10 dB multiplies the power ratio by 10. 20 dB is 100 times, not 20 times.
text.zh: 规律很好记：每加 10 dB，功率比乘 10。20 dB 就是 100 倍，不是 20 倍。

title.en: The most common mistake

body.en: Plugging 20 dB straight into the formula as S/N = 20. Convert it to 100 first, then compute $1+S/N = 101$.
body.zh: 把 20 dB 直接当成 S/N = 20 代进公式。先换算成 100，再算 $1+S/N = 101$。

title.en: Example: a 4 kHz, 20 dB channel
title.zh: 例：4 kHz、20 dB 的信道

intro.en: Go in order: units, decibels, then the formula.
intro.zh: 按顺序来：单位、分贝、代公式。

why.en: The formula needs Hz, so convert kHz first.
why.zh: 公式要 Hz，先把 kHz 换掉。

why.en: Convert decibels to a plain ratio.
Don't forget the 1 inside the brackets.
$2^6 = 64$ and $2^7 = 128$; 101 lies between them, closer to 128.

outro.en: Without a noise limit, this line could go faster just by adding levels. With 20 dB of noise, the ceiling is 26.6 kbps.
outro.zh: 没有噪声的限制时，这条线靠电平数可以更快。有了 20 dB 的噪声，上限就是 26.6 kbps。

title.en: Two limits: take the smaller

intro.en: A binary signal (V = 2) goes through a 3 kHz, 20 dB channel. How fast can it go at most? Both limits apply at once, so compute both.
intro.zh: 二进制信号 (V = 2) 通过 3 kHz、20 dB 的信道，最大能到多少？两条限制同时有效，所以两个都要算。

why.en: With only two levels, each symbol is just 1 bit.
why.zh: 只有两个电平，每个码元只有 1 个比特。

why.en: The limit allowed by noise, about 20 kbps.
why.zh: 噪声允许的上限，约 20 kbps。

why.en: The real rate cannot cross both walls at once, so take the smaller. Here the bottleneck is binary coding, not noise.
why.zh: 实际速率不可能同时越过两道墙，取小的。这里的瓶颈是二进制编码，不是噪声。

outro.en: The noise on this line would actually allow about 10 levels, so using only 2 is a waste. Switch to 8 levels and Nyquist's limit rises to 18000. Switch to 16 levels and Nyquist says 24000, but Shannon pushes it back to around 20 kbps.
outro.zh: 这条线噪声其实够分辨约 10 个电平，只用 2 个是浪费。换成 8 个电平，奈奎斯特的上限升到 18000。换成 16 个电平，奈奎斯特说 24000，但香农把它压回 20 kbps 左右。

title.en: Which wall hits first

prompt.en: A channel has a bandwidth of 4 kHz, the signal has 8 levels, and the signal-to-noise ratio is 10 dB. About what is the maximum achievable data rate in bits/sec?
prompt.zh: 一条信道带宽 4 kHz，信号有 8 个电平，信噪比 10 dB。最大可达数据速率约是多少 bits/sec？

hints.zh: 10 dB 的 S/N 是多少？

hints.en: Compute Nyquist and Shannon separately, then take the smaller.
hints.zh: 分别算奈奎斯特和香农，再取较小的。

explain.en: Nyquist: $2\times 4000\times\log_2 8 = 24000$. Shannon: $S/N = 10$, so $4000\times\log_2 11\approx 4000\times 3.459 \approx 13838$. Take the smaller: noise hits first, giving about 13.8 kbps.
explain.zh: 奈奎斯特：$2\times 4000\times\log_2 8 = 24000$。香农：$S/N = 10$，$4000\times\log_2 11\approx 4000\times 3.459 \approx 13838$。取较小的，所以是噪声先挡住，约 13.8 kbps。

title.en: Looking back at latency: how much per second versus how long to arrive
title.zh: 回头看延迟：一秒送多少，和多久到

text.en: The Physical layer lesson worked out latency. The latency L of a message has two parts:
text.zh: 物理层一课算过延迟。一条消息的延迟 L 由两段组成：

items.en: **M/R**, transmission delay: how long it takes to push M bits onto the line. R is the data rate computed in this lesson.
items.zh: **M/R**，传输延迟：把 M 个比特推上线要多久。R 就是这一课算的数据速率。

items.en: **length/speed**, propagation delay: how long the signal takes to travel the line. In cable the speed is about 2/3 of the speed of light, roughly $2\times 10^8$ m/s.
items.zh: **长度/速度**，传播延迟：信号在线上走完要多久。线缆里大约是光速的 2/3，约 $2\times 10^8$ m/s。

text.en: Example: send 5000 bytes (40000 bits) over a 10 Mbit/s link that is 2000 km long. Transmission delay is $40000/10^7 = 4$ ms, and propagation delay is $2\times10^6/(2\times10^8)=10$ ms.
text.zh: 例：用 10 Mbit/s 的链路发 5000 字节 (40000 比特)，线长 2000 km。传输延迟 $40000/10^7 = 4$ ms，传播延迟 $2\times10^6/(2\times10^8)=10$ ms。

title.en: Don't mix up the two questions

body.en: The capacity formula answers 'how many bits can go per second'; the latency formula answers 'how long until the first bit arrives, and until the whole message is sent'. Raising R tenfold only shrinks M/R and does nothing for the 10 ms of propagation delay.
body.zh: 容量公式回答「一秒能送多少比特」，延迟公式回答「第一个比特多久到、整条消息多久送完」。把 R 提高十倍，只缩短 M/R，对 10 ms 的传播延迟毫无办法。

title.en: Compute the latency of a message

prompt.en: A link has a rate of 20 Mbit/s and is 1000 km long (signal speed $2\times10^8$ m/s). A message of 25000 bytes is sent. What is the latency L in milliseconds?
prompt.zh: 链路速率 20 Mbit/s，长 1000 km (信号速度 $2\times10^8$ m/s)，发一条 25000 字节的消息。延迟 L 是多少毫秒？

hints.en: Transmission delay = M/R, propagation delay = length/speed.
hints.zh: 传输延迟 = M/R，传播延迟 = 长度/速度。

explain.en: Transmission delay $200000/(20\times10^6)=10$ ms, propagation delay $10^6/(2\times10^8)=5$ ms, total 15 ms.

title.en: Three link directions

text.en: On one link, can the machines at the two ends talk at the same time? Two questions settle it: can it go both ways? Can it go at the same time?
text.zh: 同一条链路上，两端的机器能不能同时说话？看两个问题就能判断：能不能双向？能不能同时？

alt.en: Three rows: full-duplex has two arrows at once; half-duplex has one solid and one dashed arrow taking turns; simplex has a single arrow
alt.zh: 三行图：全双工两个箭头同时存在；半双工一个实线一个虚线轮流；单工只有一个箭头

caption.en: Three kinds of link between A and B.
caption.zh: A 与 B 之间的三种链路。

rows.en: A network cable where one twisted pair only sends and another only receives
rows.zh: 网线里一对双绞线专管发、另一对专管收

rows.en: A walkie-talkie, where you hold the button to speak; on one wireless channel, senders take turns
rows.zh: 对讲机按住才能说话；同一个无线信道上，发送方轮流发

rows.en: A radio station to a radio; the key signal from a keyboard to a computer
rows.zh: 广播电台到收音机；按键的信号从键盘送到电脑

text.en: Why must half-duplex take turns? Both directions share one medium and one band of frequencies, so the signals pile on top of each other and interfere, and no one can hear anything clearly. Full-duplex gives each direction its own separate path (another pair of wires). Simplex is uncommon in practice, because most communication needs the other side to answer.
text.zh: 半双工为什么要轮流？两个方向挤在同一条介质、同一段频率上，信号会叠在一起互相干扰，谁也听不清。全双工则是给每个方向各留一条独立的路 (另一对线)。单工现实里不常见，因为多数通信都需要对方回话。

title.en: Match the scenario to the direction

prompt.en: Which of the following pairings is correct?
prompt.zh: 下面哪一组配对是正确的？

label.en: A walkie-talkie where you hold the button to speak: full-duplex
label.zh: 对讲机按住按钮才能说话：全双工

feedback.en: You send only while holding and receive only after letting go, so the two directions cannot be used at once. That is half-duplex.
feedback.zh: 按住才发、松开才收，两个方向不能同时，这是半双工。

label.en: A network cable with one twisted pair only sending and another only receiving: full-duplex
label.zh: 一对双绞线专管发、另一对专管收的网线：全双工

label.en: A radio station and a radio: half-duplex
label.zh: 广播电台与收音机：半双工

feedback.en: The station only sends and the radio only receives, so the direction is fixed and never goes both ways. That is simplex.
feedback.zh: 电台只发、收音机只收，方向永远固定，没有双向，这是单工。

label.en: A laptop and a router taking turns to send on one wireless channel: simplex
label.zh: 同一个无线信道上笔记本与路由器轮流发：单工

feedback.en: Both directions can be used, just not at the same time. That is half-duplex. Simplex means only one direction, always.
feedback.zh: 两个方向都能传，只是不能同时，这是半双工。单工是永远只有一个方向。

explain.en: The way to decide is two questions: can it go both ways? Can it go at the same time? Only if both are yes is it full-duplex.
explain.zh: 判断的办法是两问：能不能双向？能不能同时？两个都能，才是全双工。

title.en: Why not run a separate wire to everyone
title.zh: 为什么不给每个人拉一根线

text.en: Hundreds of people in a dorm building get online, yet only one optical fibre leads to the campus network. A separate wire for each person means digging trenches, laying cable and spending money; and with wireless there is only one slice of air, which cannot be split apart.
text.zh: 宿舍楼里几百个人上网，却只有一根光纤通向校园网。给每人单独拉一根线，要挖沟、要布线、要钱；空中的无线更是只有一片，没法分开。

text.en: The answer is to let many people share the same medium, which is called **multiplexing**: dividing the capacity of one channel among several users. The question is how to divide it. There are two basic ways to slice it: by time, or by frequency.
text.zh: 办法是让很多人共用同一条介质，这叫 **多路复用** (multiplexing)：把一条信道的容量分给多个用户。问题是怎么分。有两种基本切法：按时间切，或者按频率切。

title.en: The two greyed-out items in the slides

body.en: The slides also list statistical multiplexing and CDMA, but they are greyed out; these notes do not cover them, and they are not tested in this lesson. Their starting point comes up later: whoever has data is the one who uses the channel.
body.zh: 课件还列了统计复用 (statistical multiplexing) 和码分多址 (CDMA)，但画成灰色，这份讲义不讲，也不是这一课的考点。它们的出发点后面会遇到：谁有数据谁才占用信道。

title.en: Time-division multiplexing: taking turns on the whole channel
title.zh: 时分复用：轮流占用整条信道

text.en: Time-Division Multiplexing (TDM): time is cut into slots, and users 1, 2, 3 send in turn on a fixed schedule. Whoever's turn it is gets the full speed of the channel to themselves.
text.zh: 时分复用 (Time Division Multiplexing, TDM)：把时间切成一个个时隙 (slot)，按固定时间表，用户 1、2、3 轮着发。轮到谁，谁就独占信道的全速。

alt.en: At the top, slots for users 1, 2, 3 in turn with gaps between them; below, user 2's slots are empty
alt.zh: 上方三个用户的时隙按 1、2、3 轮流排列，槽间有空隙；下方用户 2 的时隙空着

caption.en: The schedule is fixed; an empty slot is not given to anyone else.
caption.zh: 时间表是固定的，空槽不会让给别人。

text.en: Why is a **guard time** needed? Users' clocks always have a little error, and signals do not all take exactly the same time to arrive. If slots sit end to end, a slight misalignment makes the data of two neighbouring users collide. A gap leaves room for those errors.
text.zh: **保护时间** (guard time) 为什么要留？各用户的时钟总有一点误差，信号传到的时间也不完全相同。如果槽首尾紧挨，一点点错位就会让相邻两个用户的数据撞在一起。留一段空隙，就是给这些误差留余地。

text.en: The cost of a fixed schedule is also in the picture: when user 2 has no data, its slot stays empty, no one else can use it, and the channel is wasted.
text.zh: 固定时间表的代价也在图里：用户 2 没数据时，它的时隙空着，别人也用不了，信道白白浪费。

title.en: Frequency-division multiplexing: each person gets a fixed band
title.zh: 频分复用：每人一条固定的频带

text.en: Frequency-Division Multiplexing (FDM): the available frequencies are cut into several bands, and each user may use only their own, but can send continuously without waiting for a turn. The cost is that each person's bandwidth B is smaller, so by the Nyquist and Shannon formulas the rate is lower than having the whole channel to yourself.
text.zh: 频分复用 (Frequency Division Multiplexing, FDM)：把可用的频率切成几条带，每个用户只许用自己那一条，但可以连续地发，不用等轮次。代价是每人的带宽 B 变小，由奈奎斯特和香农的公式，速率就比独占整条信道慢。

alt.en: Top: three users in three bands with guard bands between; bottom: voice, upstream and downstream bands on an ADSL phone line
alt.zh: 上图三个用户占三条频带，之间有保护带；下图是 ADSL 电话线上语音、上行、下行三段频带

caption.en: On one phone line, voice, upstream and downstream each take a stretch of frequencies.
caption.zh: 同一条电话线，语音、上行、下行各占一段频率。

text.en: A **guard band** does the same job as guard time: the edges of neighbouring bands are not cut exactly flush, and a stretch of unused frequencies is left to avoid crosstalk.
text.zh: **保护带** (guard band) 的作用和保护时间一样：相邻两条频带的边缘不会刚好切齐，留一段空着的频率，免得互相串扰。

text.en: ADSL, covered in the previous Physical layer lesson, is frequency-division multiplexing: on one phone line the lowest stretch goes to voice, and the two stretches above are split between upstream and downstream. All three work at the same time and continuously, without disturbing each other.
text.zh: 上一课物理层讲过的 ADSL 就是频分复用：一根电话线上，最低的一段给语音，上面的两段分给上行和下行，三者同时、连续地工作，互不打扰。

title.en: TDM and FDM side by side

rows.en: The full speed of the channel, but in bursts
rows.zh: 整条信道的全速，但断断续续

rows.en: A continuous flow, but only a narrow band, so a lower rate
rows.zh: 连续不断，但只有一条窄带，速率较低

rows.en: Guard time; slots with no data sit empty
rows.zh: 保护时间；没数据的槽白空着

rows.en: Guard bands; bands with no data sit empty
rows.zh: 保护带；没数据的频带白空着

rows.en: Digital data (cut into packets sent by slot)
rows.zh: 数字数据 (切成包按槽发)

rows.en: Analogue signals (radio, television, voice in ADSL)
rows.zh: 模拟信号 (电台、电视、ADSL 里的语音)

text.en: Both are fixed allocations: who may send, and when or on which frequencies, is arranged in advance. The advantages are simplicity and no mutual interference; the drawback is that when a user has no data, their share simply sits idle.
text.zh: 两种都是固定分配：谁在什么时候或什么频率上可以发，事先排好了。优点是简单、互不干扰；缺点是用户没有数据时，分给他的那份就白白空着。

title.en: Where does the empty slot go

prompt.en: Three users A, B, C share a line with time-division multiplexing, taking turns in the fixed order A, B, C. In one round B has no data to send. What happens to B's slot?
prompt.zh: 三个用户 A、B、C 在一条线上用时分复用，按 A、B、C 的固定顺序轮流。某一轮里 B 没有数据要发。B 的时隙会怎样？

label.en: A and C take it and send a bit more
label.zh: 被 A 和 C 拿去多发一点

feedback.en: The schedule is fixed, so slots are not reassigned on the fly. Allocating on demand is a different approach (statistical multiplexing).
feedback.zh: 时间表是固定的，时隙不会临时重新分配。按需分配是另一种做法 (统计复用)。

label.en: It stays empty, nobody else can use it, and that stretch of channel is wasted
label.zh: 空着，别人也用不了，这段信道被浪费

label.en: The guard time gets longer to fill in the gap
label.zh: 保护时间变长，补上这段空白

feedback.en: Guard time is there to cope with clock errors and propagation differences, and has nothing to do with whether there is data.
feedback.zh: 保护时间是为了防时钟误差和传播差异，与有没有数据无关。

label.en: It automatically becomes frequency-division, and B keeps a narrow band
label.zh: 自动改成频分，B 继续占一个窄频带

feedback.en: Time-division and frequency-division are two different ways of slicing and do not convert into each other on their own.
feedback.zh: 时分和频分是两种不同的切法，不会自己互相转换。

explain.en: That is the cost of a fixed schedule: with no data the slot still exists, and still sits empty.
explain.zh: 固定时间表的代价就是这个：没数据时，时隙照样存在，也照样空着。

title.en: The whole story

text.en: A 3 kHz telephone line. **Nyquist** first works out the limit with no noise: at most $2B = 6000$ symbols per second, each carrying $\log_2 V$ bits, so the rate is $2B\log_2 V$. To go faster, add levels.
text.zh: 一条 3 kHz 的电话线。**奈奎斯特** 先算没有噪声时的上限：每秒最多 $2B = 6000$ 个码元，每个码元装 $\log_2 V$ 个比特，所以是 $2B\log_2 V$。想更快就加电平。

text.en: **Shannon** brings the noise in: when levels are packed too close, noise muddles them. The limit becomes $B\log_2(1+S/N)$, where S/N is a power ratio, and when a problem gives dB you first convert it with $10^{\text{dB}/10}$. Both limits must hold, so take the smaller.
text.zh: **香农** 把噪声放了进来：电平挤得太近，噪声就把它们搅混。上限变成 $B\log_2(1+S/N)$，其中 S/N 是功率比，题目给 dB 时要先换成 $10^{\text{dB}/10}$。两个上限都要守，取较小的。

text.en: Finally, many people share the line: **time-division** has everyone take turns with the full speed of the channel and needs guard time; **frequency-division** has everyone use their own narrow band at the same time and needs guard bands. Both are fixed allocations, and when a user has no data, that share is wasted.
text.zh: 最后，很多人共用这条线：**时分** 让大家轮流占用整条信道的全速，要留保护时间；**频分** 让大家同时占用各自的窄频带，要留保护带。两种都固定分配，用户没数据时那份就浪费了。

text.en: A link has a direction (full-duplex, half-duplex, simplex) and also a latency. Capacity says how much goes per second; latency says how long until it arrives. From the next lesson we leave the wire itself and look at how two neighbouring machines get a frame of data across reliably.
text.zh: 链路有方向 (全双工、半双工、单工)，也有延迟。容量说的是一秒送多少，延迟说的是多久到。下一课起，我们离开线本身，看相邻两台机器怎样把一帧数据可靠地送过去。
